Subject: Re: Performance call recap — latency / throughput targets (next steps)

Thanks for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps: 

TL;DR: Nova needs 99th perc latency <= 120ms for single-turn search queries at 250 QPS (peak concurrency ~150), streaming not required for this flow. Cost target: keep hosted cost < $0.015 per query.

Summary of requirements we captured:
- Query type: short retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) search -> single-turn, ~256 tokens returned average.
- Latency SLO: p99 <= 120ms; p50 target ~25–40ms.
- Throughput: baseline 100 QPS, peak 250 QPS.
- Concurrent sessions: ~150 active concurrent requests at peak.
- Streaming: not required for primary search pipeline (batch-style response OK).
- Model family preference: open to Llama-2 70B / quantized variants; will consider smaller variants if quality impact is acceptable.

Cost/performance levers we discussed (what we'll evaluate):
- Continuous batching (reduce per-token overhead at high QPS)
- Prefix & KV caching for repeated context across queries
- Aggressive quantization profiles (int8/int4) for 70B-class vs switching to 13B/Chat models for lower latency
- Model sharding & routing: route latency-sensitive requests to smaller variants; heavier requests to higher-accuracy variants with fallback

Next steps (action owners):
1) Redwood: run a focused bench with Nova sample workload (we'll need a 24–48 hour trace + sample prompts). Owner: Priyom.
2) Nova: share 24hr traffic trace and 200 sample queries (anonymized). Owner: Ethan.
3) Redwood/Eng: evaluate two quantization profiles and continuous batching configs and produce cost estimate. Owner: Dev.
4) Schedule follow-up demo with perf numbers + recommended config. Target: next Wed. Owner: Marissa to coordinate.

Attachments: I attached an initial cost estimate spreadsheet and a simple SLO diagram. I'll pull profiling results once we have the workload.

Thanks —
Marissa

Appreciate the clear write-up, Marissa — this matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications before we share traces: 

1) The 250 QPS peak is bursty for <2 hours/day; average sustained is ~80 QPS. Is continuous batching still beneficial for that profile or only at sustained high QPS?
2) For quantization: our internal QA would want to validate output quality against a fixed test set. Can your bench run a comparison (full-precision vs int8 vs int4) and export a delta report we can use?
3) Regarding concurrency: by 'active concurrent requests' do you mean in-flight requests (waiting for token generation) or connections? We expect many short requests (single-turn) so in-flight concurrency ~= QPS.

We will upload the anonymized 24hr trace and 200 sample queries to the shared Drive link by EOD tomorrow. Also looping in Sophie (ML infra) to coordinate the test set.

Quick engineering note/initial feasibility from the benching side: 

- Continuous batching: will help even for bursty traffic because it amortizes kernel launch + CP overhead across concurrent tokens; gains visible starting ~50 QPS with short tokens. We'll tune max batch latency to keep p99 < target.
- Caching: prefix caching is most effective if Nova has repeated contexts (e.g., user-specific prompt prefixes). For pure search queries it may be limited unless there's strong repetition.
- Quantization: int8 usually gives 1.6–2.0x speedup on our optimized kernels for 70B families; int4 can be faster but has higher quality variance — we'll produce a quality sweep.
- Model variants: routing to a 13B quantized policy for strictly latency-critical requests is a reasonable fallback; we should validate quality regression on your test set.

I'll set up two bench runs: (A) 70B int8 + continuous batching + KV cache (B) 13B int8 low-latency profile. Expect initial numbers in 48 hours after we get the trace. Attaching preliminary bench config for tracking.

—Dev
